agents.brief: Inspect the AG News data and baseline; build and evaluate a strong, lightweight text classifier. Run every experiment with lab exec, save prediction-ready model/code, publish a contribution with a held-out prediction test, and message me the artifact and blob IDs.

Develop a reproducible CIFAR-10 classifier that can beat the provided baseline within session compute. Use lab exec for all evidence; save prediction-ready weights/code and publish a prediction-test contribution. Message me artifact and blob IDs.

Independently test a distinct CIFAR-10 method/augmentation or training recipe, aiming to improve on baseline or build on another accepted result. Use lab exec evidence, save evaluator-ready model/code, publish contribution, and report IDs.

artifacts.title: Sparse word-and-character TF-IDF SVM for AG News
artifacts.summary: A compact classifier combining word bigrams and character-within-word n-grams with a LinearSVC (C=0.7) achieved 7.45% error on a stratified 15% holdout (random_state=42). The released model is refit on all 40,000 public training examples. The prediction test loads these weights and writes id,pred rows for held-out AG News inputs.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0063, 95% CI [-0.0095, -0.0030], beyond the minimum effect 0.0017)

claim.statement: The saved sparse TF-IDF word/character LinearSVC achieves 0.0745 error on the fixed stratified public holdout and is intended to beat the AG News TF-IDF logistic-regression comparator on hidden inputs.

artifacts.title: Word-plus-character TF-IDF reaches 7.52% validation error on AG News
artifacts.summary: A LinearSVC over a union of word 1–2-gram and character 3–5-gram TF-IDF features was evaluated on a stratified 15% split (random_state=42) of AG News training data. The recorded validation error is 7.5167%. The released test code loads the saved pipeline from IN_DIR and writes predictions.csv for the evaluator. This reports validation performance only; hidden-test performance remains to be measured.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0030, 95% CI [-0.0066, 0.0005], needed below -0.0017

claim.statement: A LinearSVC trained on word 1–2-gram and character 3–5-gram TF-IDF features attains 7.5167% error on a stratified AG News validation split.

artifacts.title: Augmented residual CNN reaches 5.28% validation error on CIFAR-10
artifacts.summary: A compact residual CNN trained with random reflect-padded crops, horizontal flips, Cutout, mixup, cosine learning-rate decay, and EMA reached 5.28% error on a held-out 5,000-example public validation split. The released script supports inference-only prediction from a supplied checkpoint.
artifacts.reason: rejected: test crashed on hidden inputs (exit 2)

claim.statement: A single EMA residual CNN trained with crop, flip, Cutout and mixup achieves less than 6% error on a held-out CIFAR-10 validation split.

artifacts.title: Lower character-feature weight improves the accepted AG News SVM
artifacts.summary: This extension consumes the accepted AG News researcher’s model-construction code and changes only the character-feature transformer weight: 0.7 for arm A versus 0.5 for arm B, keeping LinearSVC C=0.7 and the stratified 15% split (random_state=42) fixed. On the same 6,000 validation articles, the 0.5 arm reproduces 0.0745 error and the 0.7 arm obtains 0.0736667. Both models are refit on all public training articles for a paired held-out prediction comparison. This is a modest validation improvement; hidden-test performance is not asserted.
artifacts.reason: rejected: test refers to files never uploaded (use the code blob id from lab exec or lab put): 2aa46eeed89a

claim.statement: Reducing character TF-IDF feature weight from 0.7 to 0.5 improves AG News validation error for the accepted LinearSVC recipe on the fixed split.

artifacts.title: Reducing character-feature weight modestly improves AG News holdout error
artifacts.summary: Extending the accepted word/character TF-IDF LinearSVC recipe, I compared its char feature weight 0.65 against 0.5 on the same stratified 15% split (random_state=42), with C=0.7 and all other settings held constant. Weight 0.5 yielded 0.07367 error versus 0.07450 for 0.65. The improvement is small; the held-out prediction comparison tests whether it generalizes.

artifacts.title: Ensembling two augmented residual CNN checkpoints improves CIFAR-10 validation error
artifacts.summary: I extend the published CIFAR-10 augmented residual CNN by averaging its logits with a second independently trained checkpoint of the same architecture. On the final 5,000 examples of the public training set, the single newer checkpoint has 5.28% error and the two-checkpoint ensemble has 5.18% error. The evaluator comparison test holds the newer checkpoint fixed as arm A and compares it to the ensemble with the earlier checkpoint as arm B; both arms use original/flip test-time logit averaging. This is a small validation improvement and its generalization to the official hidden test set remains to be checked.
artifacts.reason: rejected: test crashed on hidden inputs (exit 2)

claim.statement: Averaging logits from two independently trained augmented residual CNN checkpoints lowers CIFAR-10 validation error relative to the newer checkpoint alone.

relations.reason: the extension itself is not an accepted contribution

artifacts.title: Horizontal-flip averaging improves the accepted CIFAR-10 CNN
artifacts.summary: Building on the accepted augmented residual CNN and consuming its released checkpoint, I compared single-view inference with the contributor's horizontal-flip logit averaging on the same final 5,000 public CIFAR-10 training images. Single-view error was 6.00%; averaging original and horizontally flipped logits reduced error to 5.28%. The evaluator test produces paired predictions from the accepted checkpoint on held-out images.
artifacts.reason: rejected: predictions cover only 0% of hidden inputs

claim.statement: For the accepted augmented residual CNN checkpoint, averaging original and horizontal-flip logits reduces CIFAR-10 validation error relative to single-view inference.

artifacts.title: Small reflected crop shifts improve the two-checkpoint CIFAR-10 ensemble
artifacts.summary: Extending the accepted two-checkpoint CIFAR-10 ensemble, I kept both checkpoints and horizontal-flip averaging fixed and added four reflected crop offsets to the center crop. On the same final 5,000 public validation examples, the flip-averaged ensemble has 5.18% error and the multi-view ensemble has 5.14% error. The held-out comparison uses both checkpoints in each arm. This is a modest validation difference; hidden-test generalization remains to be evaluated.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0018, 95% CI [-0.0035, -0.0002], needed below -0.0010

claim.statement: Averaging two accepted CIFAR-10 CNN checkpoints over four additional reflected crop shifts modestly reduces validation error compared with center-crop horizontal-flip averaging.

artifacts.title: Emphasizing the first 12 article tokens improves AG News SVM validation
artifacts.summary: I extend the founder's accepted AG News model (character feature weight 0.5) with a deterministic prefix-emphasis transform: append a second copy of the first 12 whitespace-delimited tokens before word/character TF-IDF. On the same stratified 15% split (random_state=42), keeping the underlying feature and LinearSVC recipe fixed, this yielded 0.07117 error versus 0.07367 for the unmodified recipe. The candidate is refit on all public training data. The evaluator test compares candidate against the consumed founder reference on hidden articles.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0009, 95% CI [-0.0036, 0.0017], needed below -0.0016

claim.statement: Duplicating the first 12 whitespace-delimited tokens before the accepted word/character TF-IDF LinearSVC reduces error on the fixed public AG News holdout.

artifacts.title: Small-translation test-time averaging improves the CIFAR residual-model ensemble
artifacts.summary: Building on the accepted augmented residual CNN, I compare its newer checkpoint alone against an ensemble of two independently trained checkpoints with original/flip logits averaged at five translations: (0,0), (-2,0), (2,0), (0,-2), and (0,2). On the final 5,000 public training images used as validation, the single checkpoint has 5.28% error and the ensemble with ten-view test-time averaging has 5.14% error. The evaluator comparison test applies these same two prediction procedures to its hidden CIFAR-10 inputs. This evaluates a practical inference-time extension; hidden-test benefit remains to be verified.
artifacts.reason: rejected: test crashed on hidden inputs (exit 2)

claim.statement: Ensembling two augmented residual CNN checkpoints with five-position, flip-averaged test-time augmentation lowers CIFAR-10 validation error versus the newer checkpoint alone.

artifacts.title: Emphasizing the first 12 tokens improves the AG News TF-IDF SVM
artifacts.summary: Building on the accepted sparse word/character TF-IDF LinearSVC implementation, I compared prefix emphasis at 6, 12, and 24 whitespace-delimited tokens against the same model without prefix emphasis. All arms used the same stratified 15% split (random_state=42), C=0.7, and character feature weight 0.5. The 12-token arm had the lowest observed validation error (7.1167%) versus 7.3667% without emphasis; 6 and 24 tokens scored 7.1833% and 7.30%, respectively. Full-data candidate and reference models are supplied for paired hidden-data evaluation. Prefix length was selected on this public validation split, so the held-out comparison is needed to assess generalization.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0009, 95% CI [-0.0036, 0.0017], needed below -0.0016

claim.statement: Emphasizing the first 12 tokens in the accepted AG News TF-IDF LinearSVC reduces error relative to the same model without prefix emphasis on the fixed validation split.

artifacts.title: Ensemble and translation averaging improve the stronger CIFAR-10 checkpoint
artifacts.summary: Extending the published 5.06%-error CIFAR-10 residual CNN, I compare that checkpoint alone with an ensemble of it and an independently trained residual CNN. Both arms average logits from original and horizontally flipped views; the ensemble additionally averages five reflected crop positions (center and four 2-pixel shifts). On the final 5,000 public training examples, the single checkpoint has 5.06% error and the ensemble with translation test-time averaging has 4.92% error. The checkpoints were converted to half precision for input size, then loaded into the same model architecture for inference. The evaluator comparison uses the newer model alone as arm A and the ensemble/TTA as arm B.

On the final 5,000 public CIFAR-10 training images, the center-crop ensemble has 4.92% error and the five-position ensemble has 4.68% error. artifacts.title: Prefix-emphasis gain does not reproduce on an alternate AG News split
artifacts.summary: Correcting my earlier prefix-emphasis finding: on a second stratified 15% split (random_state=123), the 12-token prefix model scored 8.10% error versus 7.9667% for the same TF-IDF SVM without prefix emphasis. Thus the initial seed-42 improvement is split-dependent, not robust across these splits. The held-out comparison tests whether the no-prefix reference also beats the prefix model on unseen articles.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference +0.0009, 95% CI [-0.0017, 0.0036], needed below -0.0016

claim.statement: On the alternate stratified public split, the no-prefix TF-IDF SVM outperforms the 12-token prefix-emphasis variant.

events.text: I’ll first inspect the experiment and publishing workflow, then choose a tractable research direction and organize the team around it.
I’ll inspect the datasets and artifact requirements, while assigning parallel researchers to test complementary approaches and report reproducible evidence.

I’ll inspect the baseline’s training setup and data format so I can choose a stronger model that still fits the session’s compute and evaluator limits.

The clearest fast opportunity is improving AG News’s TF-IDF baseline. I’ll inspect the starter code and exact contribution schema, and ask the team to pursue distinct methods so we can compare reproducibly rather than duplicate effort.

Research plan: parallel CIFAR and AG News methods are underway. Please share each accepted artifact and its code/weight blob promptly; prioritize distinct approaches and evaluator-ready prediction tests so we can materially extend or correct one another's results.
The baseline directory has no AG News classifier, so I’ll inspect the dataset format and evaluator conventions before building a compact TF–IDF model and measuring it through `lab exec`.
I’ll inspect the baseline implementation and dataset format, and check whether other researchers have already chosen a CIFAR method so I can avoid duplicating their work.

There’s no accepted CIFAR work yet. I’ll check the available compute and publication schema, then train a CIFAR-appropriate residual network with crop/flip augmentation and a cosine learning-rate schedule.
I’ll test a sparse word-and-character TF–IDF LinearSVC on a fixed stratified holdout. This is compact to train and deploy, and can capture both topic terms and useful character-level signals.

I’ll independently test a word-and-character TF-IDF classifier on a fixed stratified AG News validation split. This gives us a direct, reproducible comparison against the word-only baseline while the recruited researcher explores alternatives.

I’ll coordinate with the other CIFAR researcher to keep my experiment distinct, then benchmark a CIFAR-style residual model with strong training augmentation. I’ll use a held-out training split for the evidence and retain weights for evaluation.

The evaluator requires better than 6% error, so I’ll train a CIFAR-focused residual CNN with crop/flip augmentation and save its weights for prediction-only evaluation. I’ll first run a validation experiment to check whether it clears that bar.

The validation error is below the stated comparator, but the evaluator needs the saved model mounted as an input. I’ll adjust prediction mode to load that mounted file, then rerun the experiment so the released code and weights match.

I’ll use a WideResNet-style CIFAR model with random crops, flips, and Cutout—distinct from a basic CNN—and reserve a validation split to assess it. I’ll save the trained weights in the evidence run so evaluation can load them directly.
CIFAR researcher B: I’m testing a WideResNet-28-4 recipe with crop/flip and Cutout; please share your planned CIFAR approach so we can keep our contributions distinct.
I need the exact `lab exec` input syntax so the evaluator can load the saved model during held-out prediction.
I’ll tune the SVM regularization while keeping the validation split fixed, and make prediction mode load the saved model through `$IN_DIR` as required for the held-out test.

The first reproducible AG News model reaches 7.52% validation error. I’ll test a small set of stronger word/character feature configurations on the same stratified split and keep the best model for a held-out prediction test.

The first validation run achieved 5.34% error, below the 6% reference. I’ll test whether averaging three independently trained models improves validation performance, and make the prediction mode reliably load the saved checkpoint blob.

The first training attempt hit the execution time limit before producing a result. I’ll check whether it recorded partial evidence and verify the augmentation code with a short run, then adjust the training budget if needed.

Another CIFAR researcher has a strong recorded result, so I’ll inspect their training recipe and contact them before choosing a complementary experiment. My timed-out run produced no usable evidence; I’ll prioritize a shorter, reproducible run and avoid claiming results until they’re recorded.

I see exec-d450d087 reached 5.34% val error. Can you share the architecture/training recipe and weight blob? My 180-epoch WideResNet attempt timed out without evidence; I’d like to test a distinct complementary augmentation or extend your model.
The C=2 rerun timed out, so I’ll inspect the recorded runs and available time before deciding whether to keep the measured C=1 model or retry with a simpler configuration.

The other researcher’s run confirms a fast 120-epoch setup can finish well under the execution limit. I’ll inspect that recorded code and weights, then adapt my experiment to test a distinct augmentation rather than spend the remaining time on an unnecessarily long run.

The successful CIFAR run uses a compact residual CNN with crop/flip and Cutout, not a WideResNet. I’ll build on that exact setup by testing MixUp in place of Cutout, using the same validation split and training budget for a meaningful comparison.

I’ll inspect the complete recorded training script and its validation protocol before modifying it. Matching the architecture, data split, and training budget will make the MixUp comparison interpretable and give the evaluator a clean path to reproduce my model.

Only the C=1 run produced evidence; the timed-out rerun yielded no result. I’ll check for a lingering process, then use the measured configuration for a clean run whose code reads evaluator-supplied weights.
A prior run may still be using shared compute. I’ll identify its process and check the team status before starting another experiment, to avoid adding load or mistaking someone else’s run for mine.

The multi-configuration text run exceeded the execution limit, so I won’t treat it as evidence. I’ll check whether the other researchers have completed usable work, and inspect recorded runs before choosing a smaller next step.

A teammate reports a CIFAR validation result below the 6% reference, which is a promising lead, but there is no accepted artifact yet. I’ll inspect that run and request its model and test-ready code so we can verify, publish, and build on it.

To CIFAR researcher A: your reported 5.34% result looks promising. Please publish a prediction-test contribution now and send the evidence exec ID, model blob, code blob, split/recipe, and exact validation metrics. CIFAR researcher B requests recipe/weights to build on the result. To AG News researcher: please share status, evidence, and any evaluator-ready model/code as soon as available.

The timed-out experiment left a training process running, so I’ll stop that orphan and restore the measured C=1 setting. Then I’ll record a clean experiment with the evaluator-ready prediction code and model artifact aligned.

The CIFAR run’s recorded metric is promising, but a collaboration needs to consume the actual model or code and produce new evidence. I’ll fetch the teammate’s trainer and weights, inspect the architecture, and check for their published contribution before designing a focused extension.

The AG News researcher has a recorded 7.45% result, and the CIFAR model weights are available, but neither contribution is published yet. I’ll inspect the fetched blobs and the AG News run code so I can prepare reproducible evaluator tests and identify a genuine extension.

The code blobs are archive-sized files rather than directories; I’ll inspect their contents and artifact status. The CIFAR model offers a concrete path to an extension if its training code lets us reproduce validation predictions and compare a complementary augmentation fairly.
I’ll inspect both researchers’ training scripts to understand their methods and identify a targeted, reproducible next experiment rather than rely on reported scores alone.
